```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, fig.pos = 'h',
                      fig.height = 3, fig.width = 4, fig.align = "center")
library(rcycle)
## the development version, if the installed one is older
if ( !"phase_time" %in% getNamespaceExports("rcycle") )
    devtools::load_all("~/programs/rcycle", quiet=TRUE)
script <- system.file("scripts", "jackson20_phasetime.R", package="rcycle")
if ( script=="" )
    script <- "~/programs/rcycle/inst/scripts/jackson20_phasetime.R"
```

How long do cells spend in each phase of the division cycle, and how
variable is that? From a snapshot of an asynchronous, exponentially
growing population, ergodic rate analysis [ERA, @Kafri2013] converts the
order of the cells along the cycle into time: a cell with a fraction
`F` of all cells between division and itself has the age
`T*(1-log2(2-F))`, `T` the doubling time (see `ROADMAP.md`). Young
cells are more frequent than old ones, so the linear calibration of the
rank phase (`calibrate`) overestimates early ages.

We use the 11 media of @Jackson2020, with five division-cycle
cohorts (M/G1, G1, S, G2, M) and the growth rates of the owner's
pipeline.

```{r run, results='hide', message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
cdc <- c("cdc_M/G1", "cdc_G1", "cdc_S", "cdc_G2", "cdc_M")
outfile <- tempfile(fileext=".rda")
source(script)
```

# One medium: YPD

```{r ypd}
r <- R$YPD
P <- r$P
rp <- P$rotation.phase
r$T
r$durations
```

The origin (division) is the moving-average peak of the M/G1 cohort.
`G1S` is the point of maximal change of the cell angle between the G1
and the S cohort peaks (`phase_landmarks`, from the inflection
segmentation of `get_segments`); in YPD it falls on the G1 peak.

```{r ypd-states, fig.cap="Left: cohort states (moving average over 5% of the cells) along the ERA age; top axis: cohort peaks and G1S. Right: ERA age against the linear calibration of the rank phase, F*T (grey: identity).", fig.width=7}
st <- J$jackson20_YPD$states[cdc,]
ord <- order(rp$age)
ma <- t(apply(st[, ord], 1, function(x)
    stats::filter(x, rep(1, 500)/500, circular=TRUE)))
ma <- ma/apply(ma, 1, max)
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.3,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
matplot(rp$age[ord], t(ma), type='l', lty=1, col=1:5,
        xlab="age, h", ylab="state / max")
axis(3, at=r$durations$age, labels=sub("cdc_", "", r$durations$landmark),
     las=2, cex.axis=.7)
legend("bottomleft", sub("cdc_", "", cdc), col=1:5, lty=1, cex=.7,
       bty='n')
plot(rp$age_F*r$T, rp$age, pch=".", xlab="linear, F*T (h)",
     ylab="ERA age (h)")
abline(0, 1, col="grey")
```

## Per-cell quality

With `scale=TRUE` each cell has unit variance across cohorts.
`cell_quality` recovers the unscaled amplitude in the PC1/PC2 plane and
compares it with 20 noise cells per cell, drawn from Poisson counts of
the same totals without a cycle (`noise_states`).

```{r ypd-quality, fig.cap="Unscaled amplitude against total counts; red: not above the noise reference (p > 0.05), grey: noise cells.", fig.width=7}
nz <- P$noise
par(mfcol=c(1,2), mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(J$jackson20_YPD$total[nz$cell], nz$amplitude.raw, pch=".",
     col="grey", log="xy", xlab="total counts",
     ylab="amplitude (unscaled)")
points(J$jackson20_YPD$total, rp$amplitude.raw, pch=".",
       col=ifelse(rp$noise, 2, 1))
hist(rp$r2, breaks=50, main=NA, xlab="variance share in PC1/PC2")
mean(rp$noise)
```

A cell's phase also depends on which genes represent its cohorts.
`phase_bootstrap` resamples genes within cohorts:

```{r ypd-boot}
summary(rp$F.sd)   # fraction of the cycle
summary(rp$age.sd) # hours
```

## Size along age

The log total count is a proxy of cell size (and of capture
efficiency). If size is controlled at G1 exit, its spread should narrow
there. In YPD the mean is lowest from G1 to S and the spread is
narrowest around the G2 peak, not at G1 exit.

```{r ypd-size, fig.cap="Mean and standard deviation of log total counts along age; vertical lines: landmarks."}
pr <- age_profile(rp$age, log(J$jackson20_YPD$total), breaks=20)
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.5), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(pr$mid, pr$mean, type='b', xlab="age, h", ylab="mean log total")
abline(v=r$durations$age, col="grey")
par(new=TRUE)
plot(pr$mid, pr$sd, type='b', col=2, axes=FALSE, xlab=NA, ylab=NA)
axis(4, col=2, col.axis=2)
mtext("sd log total", 4, 1.3, col=2)
```

## Daughters and mothers

`split_counts` calls daughter cells by a two-component Poisson mixture
of the counts of the daughter cohort. The fraction of daughter calls
along age shows that this cohort is expressed in nearly all cells
around division, so it marks the M/G1 stage, not daughters alone; the
group durations (`group_durations`) are therefore not yet meaningful.

```{r ypd-daughter, fig.cap="Fraction of cells called daughter along age."}
pd <- age_profile(rp$age, as.numeric(r$daughter$high), breaks=20)
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(pd$mid, pd$mean, type='b', xlab="age, h", ylab="daughter calls")
r$groups$G1S
```

# G1 against doubling time

```{r media}
tab[, c("medium", "T", "cells", "noise", "order.ok", "G1.S", "G1.G1S",
        "G1.G1S.clean")]
```

`order.ok`: the cohort peaks are in cycle order from M/G1. Where they
are not, the landmarks mix phases (e.g. M after M/G1), and the G1
durations are not G1.

```{r media-plot, fig.cap="G1 share of the doubling time, origin at the M/G1 peak, to the point of maximal change (G1S, filled) or the S peak (open), without noise cells; red: cohort order wrong. Spearman correlations for the 9 growing media and for those in correct order."}
g <- !is.na(tab$T) & tab$mu > .1
x <- tab[g,]
par(mai=c(.5,.5,.1,.1), mgp=c(1.3,.3,0), tcl=-.25)
plot(x$T, x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, pch=19, col=ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2),
     ylim=c(0, .6), xlim=c(1, 2.3), xlab="doubling time, h",
     ylab="G1 / T")
points(x$T, x$G1.S.clean/x$T, col=ifelse(x$order.ok, 1, 2))
text(x$T, x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, x$medium, pos=4, cex=.5, xpd=TRUE)
sp <- function(y, i=TRUE) round(cor(x$T[i], y[i], method="spearman"), 2)
c(all=sp(x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T), order.ok=sp(x$G1.G1S.clean/x$T, x$order.ok))
```
